subject: Anna Callahan City Council Candidacy
overview: Hosts interviewed City Council candidate Anna Callahan about her professional background in software and political organizing. Callahan outlined a platform focused on community engagement, climate resilience, housing, and progressive financial reform.

items.title: Candidate background and political journey
items.summary: Anna Callahan introduced herself as a former software engineer who transitioned into political organizing and training after the 2016 presidential election.

items.title: Local policy priorities
items.summary: Callahan identified housing affordability, climate retrofitting, road and sidewalk repairs, and school funding as her primary policy objectives.

items.title: Community engagement and outreach strategy
items.summary: The candidate proposed holding multiple weekly listening sessions within the community to engage marginalized voices and residents who typically do not vote in local elections.

items.title: Equity and city liaisons
items.summary: Callahan discussed the importance of supporting existing community liaisons and fostering cultural integration that avoids erasing the identity of marginalized groups.

items.title: Regional public bank proposal
items.summary: Callahan proposed exploring a regional public bank for Massachusetts cities to reduce debt service costs and keep taxpayer interest payments local rather than paying fees to Wall Street.

items.title: Vision for community organizing
items.summary: The candidate shared a vision for resident-led initiatives, such as 'depaving parties' and neighborhood tree-planting projects, to improve the city through collective action.

items.title: Campaign kickoff announcement
items.summary: Callahan announced an upcoming campaign kickoff event featuring music and childcare to encourage family participation.
